reading: attention, not severity - SignalMap makes no vulnerability claim

signals.title: 2 endpoint(s) reached by 'user' that only 'admin' is offered
signals.why: two captured identities disagree about this endpoint: the lower-privileged one requested it, and nothing that identity's interface was served ever names it. That is where a broken access control would look exactly like this
signals.suggested: replay each request as the lower role and as the higher one and compare: equal bodies mean the boundary is not enforced, a denial or an empty result means it is. SignalMap has not tested this and makes no claim
signals.note: attention, not severity; SignalMap makes no vulnerability claim

signals.title: 1 model API the application refers to
signals.why: the client-side code names a model API, and a credential for one of those providers appears in the same shipped code. Together those say the key reaches the browser
signals.suggested: check whether the request is made from the browser or proxied. Providers named: OpenAI
signals.note: attention, not severity; SignalMap makes no vulnerability claim

signals.title: 4 parameters that read as object references (IDOR candidates)
signals.summary: account_id on shop.example.com/api/account/address, id on shop.example.com/api/admin/users/{id}, account_id (integer) on shop.example.com/api/export, id (integer) on shop.example.com/api/orders/{id}
signals.why: an id a client supplies is where a missing per-object authorization check shows up - a reading of the parameter's name and value shape, never a claim
signals.suggested: confirm the check that should bound this input, with an authorized test
signals.note: attention, not severity; SignalMap makes no vulnerability claim

signals.title: 2 endpoints refused an anonymous request (401/403)
signals.why: the endpoint itself refused the scan for lack of credentials - the clearest evidence of an authorization boundary, and the surface an authenticated session would open
signals.suggested: re-scan with a session for one of these to see what it guards
signals.note: attention, not severity; SignalMap makes no vulnerability claim

signals.title: 35 entities mapped while holding your session
signals.why: this scan ran signed in, so the model describes the application a signed-in user sees - which part of it needs the session is the one thing a single run cannot say
signals.suggested: scan again without --auth-storage-state and diff the two: what only appears in this one is the authenticated surface
signals.note: attention, not severity; SignalMap makes no vulnerability claim

signals.title: 1 model-provider key in shipped code
signals.why: a OpenAI credential format appears in code the browser downloads. Unlike most credentials this one is metered and needs no access to the application to spend: whoever holds it can bill the owner directly
signals.suggested: confirm whether each is a real key or a placeholder, and whether the model call belongs on the server. SignalMap has not validated any of them against any service
signals.note: attention, not severity; SignalMap makes no vulnerability claim

signals.title: 2 endpoints referenced in source but never observed in use
signals.why: the application's own code names these, and nothing was seen calling them during this scan - the disagreement is the interesting part
signals.suggested: confirm whether these are reachable, and by whom
signals.note: attention, not severity; SignalMap makes no vulnerability claim

signals.title: 1 parameter that read as credentials carried in a URL
signals.why: a token or key in a query string ends up in logs, history and referers - a reading of the parameter's name and value shape, never a claim
signals.suggested: confirm the check that should bound this input, with an authorized test
signals.note: attention, not severity; SignalMap makes no vulnerability claim

signals.title: 1 collector did not see everything
signals.summary: browser is NOT_CONFIGURED: disabled by configuration
signals.why: every count in this scan is a floor rather than a total, and a signal that did not fire may only mean nothing looked
signals.suggested: raise the budget and re-scan before treating any absence as real
signals.note: attention, not severity; SignalMap makes no vulnerability claim

signals.title: 6 endpoints called at runtime with no source reference
signals.summary: shop.example.com/api/account/preferences, shop.example.com/api/billing/invoices, shop.example.com/api/orders/{id}, shop.example.com/api/session, shop.example.com/graphql, shop.example.com/static/app.js.map
signals.why: something requested these while the page ran, and no bundle this scan read mentions them - the caller is code that was not collected
signals.suggested: find what issues these calls; a chunk may not have been fetched
signals.note: attention, not severity; SignalMap makes no vulnerability claim

signals.title: 7 secret candidates in shipped code
signals.summary: values whose shape matches a known credential format, or whose name says so Some of these formats are publishable by design and are protected by an origin or referrer restriction rather than by secrecy - check the restriction, not the exposure.
signals.why: shape is not proof - many are publishable keys - but a credential format in client code is worth a human deciding about
signals.suggested: confirm whether each is publishable or was never meant to ship
signals.note: attention, not severity; SignalMap makes no vulnerability claim

signals.title: 1 published source map
signals.summary: the original source of 1 bundle is recoverable
signals.why: a source map turns a minified bundle back into readable code, including paths and dependency names the build intended to hide
signals.suggested: read the reconstructed tree for structure the bundle hides
signals.note: attention, not severity; SignalMap makes no vulnerability claim

signals.title: No identity providers, 1 authentication route
signals.why: how an application delegates identity shapes everything behind it
signals.suggested: the signed-in application was never observed; SignalMap does not sign in
signals.note: attention, not severity; SignalMap makes no vulnerability claim

signals.title: 4 configuration blocks served to the browser
signals.summary: the application hands its own settings to anyone who loads the page
signals.why: configuration names services, identifiers and endpoints that no crawl of the rendered page would reach
signals.suggested: read the keys for service identifiers and API bases
signals.note: attention, not severity; SignalMap makes no vulnerability claim
